html:
Sima Qian was the court historian of the Han dynasty and the author of the Records of the Grand Historian, the first great history of China. He is called the father of Chinese history writing.

He took over the post of Grand Historian from his father, Sima Tan, and promised him to finish the history he had begun. Around 99 BCE he defended the general Li Ling, who had surrendered to the Xiongnu. Emperor Wu was furious, and Sima Qian was sentenced to castration. Instead of choosing suicide, the honourable way out, he accepted the punishment so he could finish his work.

His book covers over two thousand years, from the legendary Yellow Emperor to his own day. He split it into annals of rulers, tables, treatises on things like music and the calendar, histories of noble houses, and lively biographies of all kinds of people, from generals and thinkers like Sun Tzu to assassins and merchants. This form became the model for China's official histories for two thousand years. He is often compared with the Greek Herodotus.
sum: Sima Qian was the court historian of the Han dynasty and the author of the Records of the Grand Historian, the first great history of China. He is called the father of Chinese history writing.
